rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Energy is never created or destroyed — it only changes form. The freely falling body proves it: dropped from height h, a body carries PE = mgh at the top, mgh/2 + mgh/2 halfway down, and KE = ½m(2gh) = mgh just before landing — the total stays mgh at every instant (NEB 2020, 2024). Gravity is the bookkeeper: PE drains into KE at exactly the rate height falls, so $v = \sqrt{2gh}$ is conservation solved for speed.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - KE + PE = constant (conservative forces) - mgh = ½mv² → v = √(2gh) - With friction: KE₁ + PE₁ = KE₂ + PE₂ + heat

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Mechanical vs total energy conservation:** mechanical (KE+PE) survives only conservative forces; total energy (including heat) always survives.  ·  **Energy vs momentum conservation:** both hold for isolated systems, but energy is a scalar ledger and momentum a vector one — collisions use them differently.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Mechanical energy conservation requires ALL forces to be conservative — one friction force breaks it.  ·  The reference level for gravitational PE is arbitrary — only differences matter.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Falling body table*** — mgh at top = mgh/2 + mgh/2 midway = mgh at the ground.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQs: mechanical energy of a falling body (2024, 3m); law + verification (2020, 3m).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Solve 5 free-fall problems using mgh = ½mv².  ·  Solve 5 pendulum problems finding speed at the lowest point.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Top mgh, mid mgh, ground mgh — the table is the proof."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): A 0.5 kg ball is dropped from 20 m. Find its KE and speed 5 m above the ground (g = 10).** — PE lost = mgΔh = 0.5 × 10 × 15 = 75 J = KE; v = √(2×75/0.5) = √300 = 17.3 m/s.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Most-tested: the free-fall verification (2020, 2024). Show all three positions for full marks.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **PE loss prices KE gain exactly:** v² = 2gh is energy conservation solved for speed.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Law: energy changes form; total of an isolated system is constant.  ·  Free-fall verification: top PE = mgh; mid PE+KE = mgh; ground KE = mgh — total constant throughout.  ·  Friction degrades mechanical energy to heat, but total energy still balances.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Nepal's hydropower converts falling water's potential energy to electricity — the same conservation law at national scale.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Ledger That Never Fails Energy changes form — kinetic, potential, heat, sound, light, chemical — but the total of an isolated system never changes. The freely falling body is the standard proof: mgh drains into ½mv² at exactly the rate height is lost (NEB 2020, 2024).  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts **Law of conservation of energy:** energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it only changes from one form to another — the total energy of an isolated system is constant. ### 2.1 Verification for a freely falling body (NEB 2020, 2024 — 3m) Take a body of mass m dropped from height h (air resistance neglected, ground as the zero of PE): | Position…  ·  ## 3. Worked Numericals **Q1:** A 2 kg ball is dropped from 45 m. Find its KE and speed at 20 m above the ground (g = 10). PE lost = mgΔh = 2 × 10 × 25 = 500 J = KE gained. $v = \sqrt{2KE/m} = \sqrt{500} = 22.4$ m/s. **Q2:** A pendulum bob swings; at the lowest point its speed is 3 m/s. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: In a spring-mass system, energy oscillates between kinetic and potential: ½mv² + ½kx² = constant.  ·  The work-energy theorem is more general than mechanical energy conservation — it works with friction.  ·  NEB frequently asks: 'Find the speed at the bottom' — use mgh = ½mv² for smooth surfaces.
